source: Gong prospect list. Configuration rows are reviewed transcript decisions with a catalog path and a value. Keyword matches were removed.

baseline.rule: If the prospect did not decide it, keep the Entrata factory default. Do not copy another client's agreed values.

plan.summary: One setting changes. Everything else stays on the factory default.

rows.meaning: Residents pay the processing fee on their own payments today, and she wants to keep it that way. She was checking that Entrata would not make the property pay it.
rows.setting: Require Property to Waive Convenience Fees
rows.path: Setup >> Properties >> [property] >> Financial >> Payments >> General >> Convenience Fees >> Require Property to Waive Convenience Fees
rows.does: Applies when staff record a payment for a resident in Entrata. It shows only when Allow Property to Waive Convenience Fees is on. Turned on, every staff-entered payment has its fee waived, so the property absorbs it.

options.effect: Staff-entered payments always waive the fee. The property pays it.
The resident pays the fee. Staff can still waive one when Allow is on.

reasoning: She said residents pay the fees today and asked to keep it that way.
With Yes, the property would pay the fee on every payment staff enter. That is the opposite of what she wants.
No keeps the fee on the resident. Staff can still waive one by exception.
rows.notCovered: This does not decide who pays the fee on online payments residents make themselves. That is set in the merchant account's fee setup, which is not in the 901-setting catalog. It goes to the confirm list.

rejected.setting: Allow Property to Waive Convenience Fees
rejected.why: Leave on (catalog default Yes). She did not ask to stop staff from waiving a fee for one resident.
This is for returned or reversed payments. She did not talk about that.

questions.question: Should residents pay the fee on online payments?
questions.default: Yes. Residents pay, which matches what she does today.
questions.why: This is set in the merchant account fee setup, not a property setting. She said tenants pay today. She did not say whether storage tenants pay the same way.

gaps.text: Payments must go to rent before utilities. During a Maryland eviction, an overpayment has to stay for future rent. No payment-order setting is in the catalog.

lines.text: This is the problem we're running across is if you put in utilities first then rent, then a payment's made.
It starts paying utilities even though we told the program to pay rent first.
So this is where our problem lies.
And this is, I think what arts, you know, kind of, yeah.
You guys are dictating what the charges are applied to.

gaps.text: A lump-sum move-in payment must split to the deposit ledger and still transfer on a management move. The catalog's deposit-transfer row is a different decision.

lines.text: When you mentioned deposit, when we have an applicant that becomes a resident and they pay their prorated rent and all their fees and everything, and include in one payment, their deposit problem.

We're having in real page is when we do the transfer to the deposit ledger, if the resident decides to transfer to another unit, we are stuck because that deposit is actually linked to a payment, a larger payment.
So we either have to have them pay in more on the new unit or the transferred unit or on the old unit that have balances because we can't detach the two.
Do you guys, so you guys transfer deposits between units, you don't make them pay a new deposit for the new unit?

plan.summary: No setting change yet. The closest settings do not fix his problem without a number from him.

questions.question: How many days does a turn actually take at the first property today?
questions.default: Keep the make-ready template's Days to Complete, and add the real backlog once he gives a number.
questions.why: Entrata sets a notice unit's available date to move-out plus the larger of the template's Days to Complete and 'Number Of days From Move Out Date To Show Notice Unit' (factory 0). His notice units show available too early because a backlog makes turns run longer than planned. A buffer only helps with a real number.
questions.setting: Number Of days From Move Out Date To Show Notice Unit
questions.path: S >> P >> Property >> Floor Plans & Units >> Unit Availability/Search >> Number Of days From Move Out Date To Show Notice Unit

lines.text: So, so, and I'll tell you what, what's going on with us right now for availability?
It's it's like chicken and the egg because we have us, we have a 60 day out notice to vacate, of course, right?
So we know which units are going to be vacated in the next 60 days or so, and those units are showing as available in the system for future dates for pre leasing, right?
But in many cases or in some cases, I have properties where they are backlogged because we have shortages in team members and so on or inefficiencies whatsoever.
And therefore, I have, maybe I don't know 45 days worth of make readies to complete between now and the next month and a half, how to do that.
And I am showing units that are not even vacant today, available 30 days from now.
So what's the point of having a unit that's not even vacant today, showing available sooner than one that I'm still working on.
And I'm going to finish 45 days from now, you know, so that's part of the issue that's happening.
Also what's happening is from a revenue management perspective, some of the units that are under notice right now appear to be cheaper than units that have been vacant for 120 days.
So that's also very counterintuitive.

questions.question: Which properties go on Entrata?
questions.default: The next acquisition only (fund 6). Current properties stay on RealPage.
questions.why: He said switching the current portfolio would repeat a painful migration. A new fund can be its own company.

lines.text: Yes, in a few years, but.
We are about to purchase our first property for fund number six and I think that's a pivotal point that we have right now and we've talked about this internally several times.
We want to try to avoid getting this new property or this new fund into the same master agreement with RealPage.
Because we want to have some optionality.
More than likely if we take over anything in the next 90 days, 120 days, it's going to go into RealPage.
Because we won't have enough time to settle on a better choice.

rejectedSettings.setting: Use Make Ready Date As Available On Date
rejectedSettings.why: The code already uses the later of the move-out-based date and the make-ready end date. This toggle changes the result by one day at most, so it does not fix units showing weeks early.

gaps.text: He wants to see how much is collected versus spent on each expense with a recovery (for example bulk internet), trended over time. That is reporting, not a setting.

lines.text: And… so from our side, for example, everything that's related to recoveries when it comes to utilities and all that we're now being able to build a very simple tool that can help us understand what are recoveries for every single expense, not just whatever is in with RealPage utility management.
For example, how much are we collecting versus how much are we spending on bulk internet?
So that's a very simple thing.
It's a very simple question.

gaps.text: He wants callbacks and daily volume per technician. That is reporting, not a setting.

lines.text: So they now close everything using their mobile app.
And now we know exactly who's closing, what, when, how long they're taking, how many callbacks are we having?
But that's all being built through our systems, not through one site because one site has some of this.
But for example, I cannot check how many callbacks somebody had individually.

gaps.text: Maintenance runs on paper and manager-assigned priorities. He wants each technician to have a daily sequence.

lines.text: No, I mean they do things manually.
They write things down on a piece of paper.
They have no strategy whatsoever.
They are working on whatever the manager tells them that's the priority for the day.
And I want to change that.

gaps.text: He wants capex per unit, open purchase orders, and return against underwriting. That is reporting, not a setting.

lines.text: And then obviously, so especially for our vintage of assets which is more on the eighties side, this is what we have right now.
Capex management is extremely critical because it starts to take away from the cashflow with the properties especially after a long holding period.

So managing that capex as efficiently as possible is definitely one thing that we're trying to do that's another tool that we're building or that we are working on right now to try to track exactly how much we're spending on a per unit basis, for example, how many work orders or how many service I'm sorry, purchase order are still open for a unit, whether we're spending more than what we normally would have spent… you know, anything that we're doing on that side.
So we can try to preserve cash as much as possible until we are at a point where we can potentially sell some of these assets at a profit.
